title: Crusader rolls into Libya
pull: The new Eighth Army goes for Tobruk

facts.text: Before dawn on 18 November 1941, the British Eighth Army advanced out of Egypt into Libya. Its offensive was code named Operation Crusader.
The Eighth Army was brand new. It took that name on 26 September 1941, and Lieutenant General Sir Alan Cunningham had taken command two days earlier.
The goal was to retake eastern Libya and break the siege of Tobruk, the port whose garrison had been cut off by Rommel's forces since April 1941.

The Eighth Army had about 118,000 men and more than 700 tanks, among them British Crusader cruisers, Matildas and Valentines, and American built M3 Stuarts. Sources give Rommel's German and Italian forces between about 410 and 550 tanks.
Storms the night before grounded aircraft on both sides, so German air reconnaissance did not spot the attack coming.
Alongside British units, the army included New Zealand, South African and Indian divisions.
The tank battles that followed were savage. By 21 November the 7th Armoured Brigade had only 28 of its 141 tanks still running.
A week in, General Sir Claude Auchinleck judged Cunningham too defensive and replaced him with Major General Neil Ritchie. Sources date the change to 25 or 26 November.

New Zealand troops broke through to the Tobruk garrison on the night of 26 to 27 November. Rommel lifted the siege for good on 7 to 8 December and fell back to El Agheila by the end of the year: his first defeat in North Africa.
The cost was heavy. The Eighth Army lost about 17,700 men, and the New Zealand Division suffered about a quarter of them, its costliest battle of the war.

declassified.fact: The night Crusader began, British commandos led by Lieutenant Colonel Geoffrey Keyes raided a house at Beda Littoria, far behind the lines, hoping to kill or capture Rommel. Rommel was not there. Keyes was killed on 18 November and received a posthumous Victoria Cross.

body:
Storms the night before grounded aircraft on both sides. So German air reconnaissance never saw the Eighth Army coming.

18 November 1941. Before dawn the British Eighth Army, less than two months old, advanced out of Egypt into Libya. Operation Crusader aimed to retake eastern Libya and break the siege of Tobruk, cut off by Rommel's forces since April. About 118,000 men and more than 700 tanks went forward, British, New Zealand, South African and Indian units side by side.

The tank battles were savage. By 21 November the 7th Armoured Brigade had only 28 of its 141 tanks still running. But on 7 to 8 December Rommel lifted the siege for good, his first defeat in North Africa.
